title: Trace filter combinator + keyboard shortcuts brainstorm
content:
Goal:
- Sketch a compact, keyboard-first filter composer for trace viewer that supports boolean combinators, quick presets, and keyboard nav for power users and support engineers. Prioritize discoverability + speed.

Context / why now:
- Support and SRE need to iterate fast on large trace sets (hundreds of spans) to find anomalous latencies.
- Current filter UI is click-heavy and modal-based; power users head to CLI or export traces.
- Want to reduce time-to-insight by enabling keyboard combos, inline suggestions, and ephemeral filter previews.

Design principles:
- Immediate feedback: typing a filter shows a matched span count and highlights matches in the waterfall in realtime.
- Composability: allow AND/OR/NOT groups, parentheses, and saved quick-presets.
- Keyboard-first: every action reachable by hotkeys; inline autocompletion for field names, values, and operators.
- Progressive disclosure: keep default simple (search box + quick presets), expand to advanced composer on demand.
- Predictable fallbacks: when an expression fails to parse, show inline error and a explain-to-user hint.

Key components/sketch ideas (text wireframes):
1) Compact composer bar (top of trace pane):
   [ / ]  Filter: ______________________ (match count)  [Preview] [Save]
   - Leading slash acts like "enter filter mode" (inspired by code search).
   - Typing live-filters waterfall; ESC clears.

2) Suggestion popup (autocomplete):
   - Triggered after field name or operator.
   - Items: field names (service, op, http.status, duration>, tag:<key>), recent values, snippet suggestions (e.g., "errors only").
   - Keyboard: Up/Down to pick, Tab to commit, Enter to apply.

3) Inline boolean combinator tokens (chips):
   - When user types "service:auth AND duration>200", tokens become chips for each clause.
   - Chips are editable inline (Enter opens mini-editor), backspace removes like tags.

4) Advanced composer drawer:
   - Multi-line expression editor with syntax coloring, parentheses linting, and a small grammar hint line.
   - Left column: preset toggles (errors, high-latency, cache-miss), right column: saved filters.

5) Preview mode:
   - Keyboard: Ctrl+P toggles preview. Preview overlays a shaded mask that highlights matching spans and shows a small summary card (top matches, top services).

Keyboard map (proposal):
- /  -> focus filter input (global)
- Ctrl+K -> open quick-presets menu (pallete style)
- Ctrl+P -> toggle preview highlight
- Enter -> apply filter (persist in history)
- Shift+Enter -> apply filter + open advanced drawer
- Alt+ArrowLeft/Right -> jump between prev/next applied filters in history
- ?  -> open keyboard cheat sheet overlay
- Esc -> clear filter or, if drawer open, close drawer
- Tab -> accept autocomplete suggestion

Filter grammar (user-facing syntactic sugar):
- field:value  (service:auth, http.status:500)
- field>n / field<n (duration>200ms)
- tag.key:value (tag.region:us-east)
- has:tagKey (has:trace.parent)
- error:true / error:false
- OR can be written as '||' or 'OR', AND as '&&' or 'AND', NOT as '-' prefix or 'NOT'
- Parentheses supported for grouping: (service:auth OR service:gateway) AND duration>300

Examples to include in UX copy / quick-presets:
- Errors only: error:true OR http.status:5xx
- High latency: duration>500ms
- Cold starts: duration>800ms AND span.init=true
- Cache misses: tag.cache_hit:false

Live UX behaviors / feedback details:
- Match count badge updates as typing occurs (throttled to 200ms).
- If expression incomplete (unmatched paren), show subtle red underline and a toast hint when trying to apply.
- When previewing, tooltip on hovered span shows the matching clause ("matched: duration>200ms").
- History: store last 50 applied filters per user, accessible via Ctrl+K menu. Each history item shows a small sparklines of matches over time.

Accessibility notes:
- All keyboard actions should also be reachable via ARIA-friendly controls.
- Ensure contrast on chips and highlight overlays.
- Announce match count changes to screen readers when a filter is applied.

Edge cases / open questions:
- How to handle queries that match no spans? (suggest similar, fallback to regex?)
- Should saved filters be org-scoped or user-scoped? Propose both: user-scope by default, option to publish.
- Conflict resolution for field names that are duplicated across models (e.g., tag.service vs service field). Need field scoping syntax like 'meta.service' vs 'span.service'.
- Performance: how to compute match counts quickly for large traces without full poly scan? Probe caching + prefix index. Ask infra for feasibility.
- Mobile: keyboard-first doesn't fit mobile; show simplified UI with touch-friendly chips and presets.

Backlog / tickets to create (first pass):
- UX-1: Prototype compact composer + autocomplete (mock + clickable prototype)
- ENG-1: Backend: incremental filter evaluator API + match-count endpoint (needs schema)
- SRE-1: Benchmark match-count perf on 10k/span traces (POC)
- UX-2: Keyboard cheat-sheet overlay & telemetry for shortcut usage
- UX-3: Preview overlay + tooltip "matched by"

Notes to reviewers / next steps:
- Diego: can you sketch two variants of the composer: (A) single-line tokenizing input, (B) inline mini-editor with chips?
- Nina: gather SRE input on match-count perf and index options; link results to PROD-8421.
- I'll prototype the Tab/Enter behavior in Figma and add flows for "save filter" vs "apply ephemeral".

Quick low-fi ascii examples (for sync call):
- Single-line tokenized: [Filter: service:auth] [AND] [duration>200ms]  (match 18)
- Advanced drawer:
  ---------------------------
  | Filters              [x] |
  | 1) (service:auth OR service:gw) AND duration>300 |
  | 2) error:true                                   |
  | Save to: [Personal] [Publish]                    |
  ---------------------------

Open design questions to resolve in grooming:
- Do we auto-suggest field names from trace schema? (yes, but show confidence / sample values)
- How to allow free regex vs structured filters? Offer a `raw:` prefix for regex and limit by default for safety.
- Metrics to track: time-to-first-match, shortcuts used, filters saved, preview toggles, percent of queries that hit cached counts.

References / inspirations:
- Code search UIs (slash-to-search, token chips)
- Log filter builders (e.g., Kibana) but with tight keyboard model
- Linters that offer inline fixes (use for paren suggestions)

Meeting sync agenda (30 mins):
- Quick walkthrough of sketches (5m)
- Tradeoffs of single-line vs advanced drawer (10m)
- Backend perf requirements & feasibility (10m)
- Decide owner for prototype (5m)

TODO (immediately):
- Put these sketches into a Figma page (Ava)
- Create ENG-1 ticket stub with API contract suggestions
- DM SRE channel to request quick perf notes (Nina)

Notes to self: keep this lean and avoid bloated grammar at first. We can add more operators later once infra supports efficient matching.

End of doc.
